knowledge_gaps: Mutation routing is unspecified: existing probes may call the original ModelView directly and bypass diagnostic variants. Every tested feature, readout, and scoring path needs explicit routing, with reachability witnesses kept separate from detection assertions.

The future-access mutation changes an earlier feature, but ordinary diagnostic outcomes use the final occupied position. A dedicated earlier-position causality test must observe the mutation while holding the prefix and padding fixed.

Constant features can expose history independence, but low sensitivity is not a labeled implementation fault in the unmodified checkpoint. Unchanged and identity-hook executions establish consistency; they do not establish that the original model is fault-free or provide general false-positive estimates.

Detection rules, mutation strengths, fixed constant-feature construction, expected fault-by-probe outcomes, and rate denominators are missing. Sixteen users sharing one mutation are correlated test cases, not sixteen independent faulty implementations; conditional detection rates also need coverage and uncertainty.

Calibration risks shortcut detection if faults are obvious or thresholds are tuned on the same examples. Predeclared alarms and separate calibration and assessment cases are needed. The claimed difficulty of 4 appears optimistic given routing, independent witnesses, execution-state restoration, and budget enforcement.

The proposal does not calibrate activation-patch localization itself or verify exported-predictor parity. It also lacks a demonstrated path to improved host macro validation HR@10. The 20-second allocation needs operation limits and synchronized GPU timing; restoration time must remain available.
